property_summary: selfdestruct via sudicideAnyone reverts for any caller who is not the smartfix owner
If the call to c.sudicideAnyone() does not revert, then the caller must be the smartfix_owner.
If the call to sudicideAnyone does not revert, the caller must be the owner; otherwise, the caller may or may not be the owner.
If sudicideAnyone does not revert, the caller must be the smartfix_owner.

Only the smartfix_owner (original deployer) can successfully call sudicideAnyone() without reverting; the buggy tautology allows any caller to execute selfdestruct, so the property 'the caller must be smartfix_owner or the call reverts' holds for the reference but fails for the mutant.
After a successful call to sudicideAnyone, the remaining ETH should be sent to msg.sender; the bug sends it to smartfix_owner instead, so for msg.sender != smartfix_owner the balances differ.

When sudicideAnyone is called by a non-owner, the correct contract always reverts, but the buggy contract also always reverts; when called by the owner, the correct contract selfdestructs sending all ETH to msg.sender, whereas the buggy contract selfdestructs sending all ETH to smartfix_owner, so if msg.sender == smartfix_owner and a separate receiver can be forced to fail, the ETH delivery differs.

After a successful call to sudicideAnyone (which selfdestructs), if the beneficiary is an adversarial contract that reverts in its receive, the correct version sends ETH to msg.sender causing no revert, while the buggy version sends ETH to smartfix_owner, causing the beneficiary's revert to propagate back to the caller, so the call's success status differs when msg.sender != smartfix_owner and the caller is the owner.

When the owner calls sudicideAnyone and the beneficiary is a contract that reverts in receive, the reference C's call always succeeds (because it sends to msg.sender who is the owner and presumably doesn't revert), but the buggy version sends to smartfix_owner which may be a revert-causing contract, making the call revert when smartfix_owner != msg.sender.
